headline: External references and complementary modalities fill gaps in data-limited cancer prediction
label: Cross Modal Cancer Prediction
summary: Recent work fuses methylation atlases, scDNA clones, histopathology and evolutionary features to improve cancer detection, survival and clone assignment.
synthesis: The main thread is adding information from external references or complementary modalities to cancer prediction tasks with limited data. mFrag weights cfDNA fragmentomic features with external methylation atlases for early lung cancer detection. DeSCENT derives reference-informed cellular profiles from bulk RNA-seq and adds them to TCGA survival models. SigBridgeR standardizes eight algorithms that map bulk phenotypes onto single-cell subpopulations. KLONE assigns unpaired scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq copy-number clones with an imbalance-robust per-clone k-NN ensemble. OmniT2I renders molecular profiles as images, fuses them with histopathology embeddings and infers missing modalities. EvoSurv adds a 38-dimensional evolutionary representation built from mutation burden, mutational spectra and copy-number changes to clinical and RNA data. A study of 1.3M slides measures how much sex, age and race information H&E foundation-model features carry, which bears on confounding in transferred representations. Peripheral items cover ensemble cell typing (scBoost, scDNM), hierarchical pan-cancer subtyping (HHRM) and cell calling for targeted scDNA-seq (CellSavior).
